anti_overlap: Discard stale-plan, commit-pin, dirty-tree, file-lock and strike-counter-durability findings that do not also change what a verdict is able to certify — f-001 through f-005 already hold that ground.
Discard shared-method, unverified-plate, self-authored-criteria and lane-classification findings that do not also depend on state, timing, durability, or coordination — see f-020 through f-023.
Do not resolve the tension by always preferring an isolated replay or always preferring an independent counter-assay; locate where the design chooses silently and say what the choice costs.
Do not report model routing, token pricing, prose quality, or generic workflow complexity unless coordination state and assay validity jointly make it consequential.
decision_lens: Investigate the replay-versus-independence tension without resolving it: reproducibility machinery and independence machinery are the same machinery pointed in opposite directions. Report a finding ONLY when it requires BOTH parent perspectives. Every finding must carry an intersection_justification naming the coordination fact, the assay fact, and why removing either collapses the finding entirely.
focus: Replay-versus-independence in Pattern F's verification chain: whether each mechanism that makes a re-run reproducible across fresh-context spawns is the same mechanism that makes the second examination certify nothing, and where the design settles that conflict by omission.
name: fd-fused-replay-independence
persona: Apply the perspective of a reviewer who reads a verification protocol twice — once as a distributed coordination problem (version pins, leases, durable logs, timeouts, idempotent retries) and once as an assay office (trial plate, remedy band, register, counter-assay, instrument independence) — and treats any artifact asked to serve both readings as a specification conflict until the design says which reading wins.
review_areas: Cross every durable-state need with its register role: a strike counter must reset when a plan is repaired, a plate-calibration register must be append-only across revisions — check which one the design loses by storing both in one place.

Read the verify block as two incompatible specifications at once: an idempotent retry-safe operation and an independent second examination. Ask which one Q-A is actually asking about, and whether the doc knows it is choosing.

Treat frozen criteria as a trial plate that is also a pinned read: freezing buys reproducibility across spawns and buys plate staleness at the same rate. Look for any expiry, date letter, or re-verification interval on a plan.

Classify every non-verdict — timeout, silent subagent, sandbox denial, half-applied tree — against a tolerance fixed in advance; without one, the orchestrator's default resolution of silence is an unwritten criterion.

Examine the token-share gate as both a measurement of the wrong property (weight, not fineness) and a stale partial read over asynchronously written transcripts that the measured party itself produces.

Ask what re-tests a landed PASS: 100% pre-landing assay with zero counter-assay inverts both parents' economics, and no post-landing consistency model exists to define what re-testing would even mean.

Walk one item through pin, lease, retry, timeout crossed with sample, plate, method, instrument, and register — name every cell where a coordination fix would destroy independence, or an independence fix would reintroduce drift.

severity_examples.condition: One mechanism is asked to deliver both reproducibility and independence, and no durable register exists to reveal which of the two was actually obtained.
severity_examples.scenario: The validator receives the executor's exact worktree and the executor's frozen plate, so its re-run is a perfectly idempotent retry and therefore certifies nothing; the resulting PASS is written to no durable register, so the gauge that produced it can never be assayed and a systematically wrong criterion survives all three pilots undetected.

severity_examples.condition: Silence has neither a failure-detector policy nor a remedy band, and the resolution is made by the criterion's author with no durable trace of the criterion it turned on.
severity_examples.scenario: An executor subagent never returns. The orchestrator cannot distinguish crash from slow, has no tolerance band for 'no verdict', resolves the silence itself — as the party that authored the criteria — and the two-strikes counter lives only in its context, so nothing records that the item was ever attempted.

severity_examples.condition: Frozen criteria carry neither a version pin nor an expiry, and the verdict record omits the plate's age, so staleness is unrecoverable after the fact.
severity_examples.scenario: A plan waits in the queue while a sibling session lands a change. Its frozen criteria still pass, because they were pinned to nothing and only assert what the plan itself edits; the register, if any, captures the PASS but not that the plate was a week old.

success_hints: Name the fused cell in every finding: one coordination coordinate (pin, lease, log, timeout, retry) crossed with one assay coordinate (plate, sample, method, instrument, register, remedy).
Apply the removal test: discard any finding either parent reaches alone. Bare 'no commit pin' and bare 'the validator shares the method' are parent-alone and already on the ledger as f-001 and f-020.
Prefer findings where the fix one parent demands is exactly the damage the other fears; say where the doc settles that by omission, and do not prescribe which side should win.
Check durability against reset semantics: ask what must survive an orchestrator reset, what must not survive a plan repair, and where the design keeps both in one record.
Quote the doc's own open questions (Q-A, Q-D, Q-E) where they are the conflict rather than a question, and cite line numbers from the 34-line design doc.
task_context: Review docs/brainstorms/2026-09-03-main-thread-offload-pattern-f.md (34 lines) before three pilots. Pattern F: a thin Fable orchestrator writes execution-grade plans; fresh-context Sonnet executors apply one plan and run its verify block; Opus validators re-run that same block and judge only the plan's frozen criteria; a main-thread token-share gate is measured by interstat profile.py; two-strikes escalation returns items to the orchestrator. The named tension: the machinery that makes a re-run reproducible (pinned state, frozen plate, replayed method, shared worktree, durable strike log) is the same machinery that makes a second examination certify nothing, while every independence fix reintroduces the drift that makes a verdict uninterpretable. HARD CONSTRAINT: report only findings that require BOTH perspectives, and include an intersection_justification in every finding.
